calls.head: Blackwood’s hold on the Flames won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Blackwood has been a wall against the Flames, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Flames finally get to him.

calls.head: The Avalanche should drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flames near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Colorado found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Colorado usually gets worse looks than most teams. Not tonight: an 8.8% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Four points for Cale Makar as the Avalanche beat the Flames
paras: Nathan MacKinnon got the scoring started for the Avalanche midway through the first. It was a busy second period. Martin Nečas, Artturi Lehkonen and Brock Nelson scored three goals in less than seven minutes early in the period to stretch the lead to 4-0. Joel Farabee got the Flames on the board less than two minutes later, and Martin Pospíšil cut Colorado’s lead to 4-2 early in the third. Lehkonen scored again just over two minutes later to make it 5-2 for the Avs. Cale Makar finished with four assists.

The Avalanche earned this one. Replay the chances a hundred times and they win about seven in ten. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves for the Avalanche, and Arsenii Sergeev stopped 28 of 33 at the other end.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Avalanche improved to 8-5-1, third in the Central, while the Flames dropped to 6-8-0, fifth in the Pacific.
